qt: to the Commission Mary Khan (ESN) Subject:

Several media outlets have reported that the US Department of Defence has authorised the Department of Homeland Security to test an Active Denial System (ADS) – an electromagnetic heat ray weapon1. Using a focused beam of electromagnetic waves, the system can make people feel an intense burning sensation from a distance of up to around 800 metres, thereby forcing them to retreat. This is part of the US authorities’ efforts to explore new technologies to control crowds and increase the effectiveness of border security. Given the ongoing challenges in protecting the EU’s external borders, it seems appropriate to systematically examine innovative technological options for border security at EU level as well. Modern defence systems could actively help support border guards in their work, strengthen control over Europe’s external borders and prevent unauthorised border crossings more effectively. 1.
What does the Commission make of the US’s ADS in terms of its suitability and the potential benefits for protecting the EU’s external borders?
Is it considering running testing it or similar defence systems at the EU’s external borders together with the Member States or Frontex?

What other new defence and border security systems are currently being examined by the Commission or the Member States? Which of them could be tested or deployed at the EU’s external borders in the near future?
